messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Hi — a nudge on invoice 0142, issued 12 July, now 28 days past terms. Amount is 4,150. Could you give me a payment date?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: hi! sorry, it's with finance — the september payment run is the 8th. i pushed for an earlier slot but the queue is locked

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Thanks, i can work with the 8th. Would you mind forwarding the remittance advice when it clears?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: will do, automatic

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Appreciated. Also flagging: this is the third invoice this year to run past strict terms — the previous two each went a week over. I'd like us both to stay comfortable with the arrangement.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: that's fair, and i'd rather know than wonder. the queue thing is real, the AP team shrank in may

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Thanks for being straight about it. If the september run misses, what's the escalation route — a name, an email, a ticket?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: alfred.mensah, AP lead — mention my name and doors open

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Noted, thank you. I'll also issue the current sprint on the 1st as usual, so it lands inside the same run rather than drifting.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: smart. that PO is pre-approved, i fast-tracked it myself

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Good — that keeps the ledger tidy on my end too. And thanks for the quick replies, chasing is genuinely painless when the other side shows up.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: anyway — that sprint handover doc you sent thursday was excellent, legal had zero comments

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Glad to hear it. I'd tightened the liability section after the last round of comments — that part is usually what earns the zero.

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Morning — quick check-in. Invoice 0142 shows as pending on the portal rather than scheduled, and 0143 went out friday. Different process now, or still the queue?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: good catch. portal-pending means finance has it but the run file wasn't cut yet. i'll ask alfred to confirm it's in the 8th

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Thanks. To be clear, the 8th itself is fine — it's the unknown-weeks kind of pending that makes planning hard.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: understood, i'd hate it too. let me chase before lunch

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Alfred replied — scheduled for the run, reference attached. So we're tidy again. For the next engagement i'd like to test a half-up-front term, starting small.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: half up front on the next one, sure. you're hardly a flight risk, but twelve years of agency work teaches a person things

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Exactly that. It's not about trust, it's about cash rhythm. I'll draft the terms as a one-pager this week so it isn't a surprise in september.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: send it over. legal reads fast when it's one page

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: You'll have it by thursday. And when 0142 clears, ping me — i mark things reconciled the same day, so my ledger and theirs never disagree.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: will do. genuinely sorry about the runaround this quarter

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Apology accepted, and honestly unnecessary — queues happen. Consistency is all i ask.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: consistency, coming up. the one-pager will help

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Then we're aligned on all of it.

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Morning — 0142 cleared on the 29th, thank you, the reference matched. Two things for the next phase: the rate review we discussed in june, and whether you can commit to a minimum of 20 hours a month from october.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: cleared, great. october pilot: yes, i can get 20 hours signed off. rate review — send your sheet and i'll take it to budget

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Sheet's coming today. I've held the day rate flat for two years, so the review is really about the surcharge rules — rush work and the small-jobs admin tax.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: 'small-jobs admin tax' is a great name. legal will hate it, which is how you know it's good

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: All the better — precise dislike is how good contracts get written.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: budget meets on the 11th, so expect a decision that same week

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Works for me. One flag: if it stalls past the 15th, the october start slips a month — i'd rather say that now than renegotiate mid-flight.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: fair flag. i'll make sure it doesn't stall

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Appreciated. Also — i saw the launch date moved again. Is that real this time, or the usual ambition?

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: the date moving is basically our culture now. anyway, rate sheet goes to budget today

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Small thing to keep records clean: when the sign-off lands, drop a 'confirmed' in this thread — written receipts have rescued two invoices of mine already this year.

messages.speaker: me
messages.text: you're the most organised person i have ever owed money to

messages.speaker: them
messages.text: Occupational hazard. Talk next week.
